title: Miku's 30s Stage Mini-Play 'Encore': How Do You Join 6 Clips of 5s Each Into One Full Film With No Immersion Breaks?
summary: Feeding each clip's last frame into the next one does not work - the look drifts toward photoreal with every cut. Regenerating an anime keyframe at both the start and the end of every clip locks the style. That is what joins the 6 clips into one 31-second film: style stays put, music never jumps.
tags: 1 BGM track for the whole film
stats: First fully narrative cut: 6 anime clips of 5s each (each shot 5.17s, 672×896 vertical, 24 frames per second) joined into one coherent stage music story; final film 31.0s

The style must be locked at both ends of every shot: v1 used the previous clip's last frame as the next clip's first frame, and 5 of the 6 shots drifted from anime to photoreal ▮▮▮▮▮ → v2 regenerates an anime keyframe at the start and end of every shot (dual anchor), 0 shots drifted
Adjacent shots share one keyframe: the last frame of a shot = the first frame of the next (the same image), zero jump at the seams
Twin tails, sailor uniform, gold buttons, headphones - all 4 features match across all 6 shots, zero drift

No looped bed track. Each shot's own generated audio track is time-shifted into alignment: the BGM is at full loudness from 0s, and the loudness gap (RMS, a measure of how full the sound is) at the 5 seams is ≤0.2dB, zero jumps
findings: Key finding 1: While H3 generates anime visuals, it gradually 'photorealizes' the picture within 5 seconds; if you feed the previous clip's last frame in as the next clip's first frame, this drift passes from shot to shot - so both the start and the end of every shot must be locked with cel keyframes generated by Flux2

Key finding 2: Laying one looped BGM track under the film causes a hard jump at every loop restart (loudness drops 50% in an instant) - for seamless music across the whole film, time-shift and align each shot's own generated audio track instead
Key finding 3: Write 'quiet opening' in the prompt and H3 renders near-silence - narrative silence is unreliable; the music must be at full loudness from 0s
The full pipeline (lock composition → draw keyframes → generate shot by shot → stitch → mix) takes about 16 minutes to produce one 30s narrative film
